Two spec/code name mismatches: FR-027 still says TmsScopeResolver is (context: ToolContext) => Promise<TmsCallScope> but code uses optional context and nullable return; FR-029 says export customerScopeResolver but code exports createCustomerScopeResolver (factory). This happens even though `gh api repos/<o>/<r>/actions/oidc/customization/sub` reports `use_immutable_subject: false`; the real prefix is in that response's `sub_claim_prefix` field. Older repos (re-cinq/lore, created 2026-03) still emit `repo:re-cinq/lore:...`.

Symptom: a GCP Workload Identity binding `principal://iam.googleapis.com/projects/647955581268/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/github-actions/subject/repo:<owner>/<repo>:ref:refs/heads/main` never matches. google-github-actions/auth succeeds (the pool's condition is `assertion.repository_owner=='re-cinq'`), then the first real call fails with `permission 'iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken' denied`. It looks like IAM propagation delay but does not clear after 10+ minutes. iamcredentials/sts data-access audit logs are not enabled in re5-n8n-platform, so the logs will not show the subject.

Fix: read `sub_claim_prefix` and bind that exact subject (Otto does this in infra/terraform/recinq-test, local github_oidc_subject). Alternatively bind `principalSet://.../attribute.repository/<owner>/<repo>` like Lore's github-actions-deploy SA does, but that trusts every branch and PR of the repo, not just main.

Related facts from the same rollout (2026-09-10):
- "Lore's GKE" is n8n-cluster in project re5-n8n-platform (europe-west1, Autopilot, K8s 1.35), the same cluster as the n8n-gke kube context. It has ingress class nginx-ingress, ClusterIssuer letsencrypt-prod, external-dns watching ingresses for re-cinq.com in Cloud DNS project recinq-recaptcha, and ESO v0.12.1, which serves only external-secrets.io/v1beta1 (no v1).
- A chart that creates its own GHCR pull secret through an ExternalSecret races on the very first install into a new namespace: pods start before ESO syncs the secret, the kubelet tries an anonymous pull and GHCR returns 401 (ErrImagePull). It clears within about a minute once the secret exists, and only the first install is affected.

DESIGN CALL (diverged from the issue, user-approved): recorded billing_mode on pipeline.cluster_agents, NOT station_runs/llm_calls. The credential is a per-cluster-agent property (one LORE_AGENT_LLM_SECRET_KEY per process: CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=subscription, else=api, unset=unknown), so per-run stamping would duplicate a per-cluster fact. The by_cluster read already joins cluster_agents so the read switch is one column. Also fixes a live bug: post-cutover the central cluster-agent registers+claims, giving central runs a non-null cluster_agent_id that the old ca.name-IS-NULL proxy mis-buckets as subscription.

DEFAULT 'unknown'). ai-agent-subsystem emitting the pod's exact per-call credential remains the out-of-repo follow-up noted in the issue.

Every failed implementation-loop run since 08-28 15:37 (tasks 7db1eb04, daee5447, cea7a47c, 9ae6d656, 4bf8537a → issues #1629/#1634/#1647/#1648/#1650, all now lore:blocked) died identically: implement OK (satellite, ~25m) → validate queued 30m unclaimed (central paused, sole holder of node:validate) → reaper fails it failureClass=infra → infra is retryable so validate->implement back-edge fires → implement iteration 2 (another ~30m, prompted with the infra message as its "incoming failure") → validate queued 30m again → iteration_max → task failed, ticket lore:blocked, driver re-arms and kills the NEXT ticket the same way. ~2h and two full LLM implementations burned per ticket. Root cause: pipeline.cluster_agents.paused=true on central (issue #1654), never surfaced.

Why the tests are green: the acceptance harness (line-acceptance-harness.ts) fakes the claim by mutating the row to claimed and never wires the registry, handleClaim, claimNextStationRun or the reaper; reaper tests exercise queue-timeout only on a code-review graph whose failed edge routes forward; transition tests never feed a queue-timeout visit into a budgeted back-edge. No test composes enqueue(required_tags) × registry(tags,paused,status) × claim × reaper queue-timeout × retry edge.

Refactor plan: (1) capability gate in advanceLine beside llmGate — park (no row) when no active unpaused agent satisfies the node's tags, reaper re-drives; (2) new failure class `unclaimed` (permanent for the retry budget, own hint) instead of `infra` for queue-timeout; (3) claim route answers paused distinctly and the loop logs it once (#1654); (4) reaper takes now()/queueWaitMs via deps; (5) harness gains InMemoryClusterAgents + real claim + reap(minutes) step; (6) /api/assembly-runs/{id}/nodes projects status/required_tags/cluster_agent_id/claimed_at/failure_class.","agent_id":"a50f9f29-98c7-4a80-bb72-a7de42ed82ec","source":"memory","id":"fdf57506-ad98-49d1-9c94-b2e32d22a8f1","score":0.4841269841269841,"similarity":0.48176761101540766}]}

content.text:
**Score:** 1.000

## Context

The kick-off transcript named three options for how a customer's identity reaches the TMS. The delivered OLT TMS External API removes two of them. It authenticates with a single `x-api-key` header on every request; there is no login endpoint, no OAuth flow and no per-user credential. This was confirmed by the API guide (`api/README.md`) and the OpenAPI spec (`api/tms-openapi.json`, `components.schemas` is empty, `securitySchemes` declares only `ApiKeyAuth`). OLT issues and manages the key; re:cinq receives one and stores it in `TMS_API_KEY`.

### Customer identity to us

Who signs the customer in is open (RD-5 in `specs/support-agent-tms-access`). Whichever provider does, the authenticated identity names a user and the customer company they act for, and that company carries a TMS `customerNumber`. The resolver reads that number from the verified token on every tool call.

The stand-in login (`apps/api/src/dummyPortal/`) is an OpenID Connect provider whose access tokens carry the `customer_number` claim (`apps/api/src/oauth/customerIdentity.ts:CUSTOMER_NUMBER_CLAIM`). When the real login lands, only the claim name and the provider's discovery URL change; the resolver interface is unchanged.

### Where `customerNumber` lives

CFOAgent's shipped pattern for per-user credentials stores data in the Clerk organisation's `privateMetadata`, encrypted with `encryptField` (`re-cinq/CFOAgent lib/services/clerk.ts`, `encryption.ts`, `uniconta-session-cache.ts`). Note: CFOAgent's own architecture docs describe Secret Manager and Firestore; the code uses Clerk `privateMetadata`. This ADR cites the code, not the docs.

For Otto, the `customerNumber` rides in the access token as the `customer_number` claim (see `customerIdentity.ts`). The stand-in login writes it there; the real login is expected to do the same (RD-5). The customer company's number is not stored separately in Clerk metadata for this agent — the JWT claim is sufficient, because the stand-in's tokens are short-lived and re:cinq never persists them.

A customer mapped to the wrong `customerNumber` by the identity provider is a breach with no error message: the tool will answer with data from another customer's bookings without any indication that anything is wrong. The mapping must be verified against OLT's customer list before a live deployment.

### No active organisation

`authenticateWebSocket` returns `null` for any token that does not verify or does not carry a customer number. HAL Engine refuses the WebSocket upgrade when `auth.ws` returns `null`. The customer receives the WebSocket close code, not an application-level message. An HTTP response with a Danish `400` on the login redirect is returned by the stand-in login for a user mapped to no customer company (`apps/api/src/dummyPortal/` — token issued but connection refused at the WebSocket level).

The ticket requires a Danish refusal at both the HTTP route and the WebSocket upgrade. The WebSocket refusal is implemented (return `null` from `auth.ws`). The HTTP route's Danish message for the no-customer case is an **open condition**: the stand-in login's error message at that step has not been reviewed by a Danish speaker. See `KU-15` and `docs/danish-review.md`.

### Clerk org roles

OLT's customers create their own portal users with different roles (kick-off 2026-08-17). The TMS key is company-scoped, not user-scoped, so a user's role cannot narrow what the TMS returns — the key is the same for every user in the company. Role-based narrowing of results must happen in the support agent's own code if required. This pilot is read-only booking questions; no further narrowing is applied in the PoC.

---

**Score:** 0.523

// The claim the stand-in login writes and the mapper reads; the real login's claim name replaces it (RD-5).
export const CUSTOMER_NUMBER_CLAIM = 'customer_number';

---

**Score:** 0.515

function claimsOf({customerNumber, nonce}: TesterLogin) {
  return {
    ...(customerNumber === undefined ? {} : {[CUSTOMER_NUMBER_CLAIM]: customerNumber}),
    ...(nonce === undefined ? {} : {nonce}),
  };
}
